title: Investigating Online RL in World Models

contributions.purpose: Address the pathologies of model-based offline RL (value overestimation and limited out-of-sample exploration caused by short truncated rollouts) by enabling effective full-length rollout training without hand-crafted uncertainty penalties.
contributions.mechanism: Investigate training a recurrent policy through full-length offline rollouts inside learned world models, treating each member of a world-model ensemble as a level in the Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) framework so full rollouts are made robust without hand-crafted penalties.
contributions.evaluation: Matches online PPO performance on standard offline-RL (D4RL) benchmarks while using fewer transitions than the online algorithms are traditionally trained on; demonstrates transfer back to the original environment.
contributions.domain: Reinforcement learning (model-based / offline RL, world models)
contributions.source_quote: our contributions consist in: 1) investigating training through full-length offline rollouts to address model-based offline RL challenges

contributions.purpose: Overcome the healthy-behavior / near-optimal bias documented in standard offline-RL benchmarks (e.g. D4RL) that hampers development of generalizable methods.
contributions.mechanism: A data curation method producing a new dataset that does not exhibit the positive/healthy-state biases of previous benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative: conventional offline RL methods underperform on this dataset while the proposed method remains robust; used as the stress-test dataset in experiments.
contributions.source_quote: 2) produce a dataset that does not exhibit the biases in previous benchmarks

contributions.purpose: Provide a concrete algorithm that leverages an ensemble of world models to train a transferable policy using online-RL advances in an offline setting.
contributions.mechanism: POWER (Policy Optimization with World Ensemble Rollouts): trains a collection of world models on the same data, treats them as UED levels, and uses several UED sampling/selection methods (e.g. prioritized level replay) to choose which world model the agent interacts with at each step while training a recurrent policy.
contributions.evaluation: Outperforms standard offline RL methods on the authors' curated dataset; achieves comparable results to online PPO when trained offline on D4RL; produces diverse world models even when trained on the same data.
contributions.source_quote: 3) introduce the Policy Optimization with World Ensemble Rollouts (POWER) algorithm that utilizes several UED methods to select which world model the agent will interact with at every step.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We break the traditionally constrained setting of UED and use it to select over a large number of world models trained on the same dataset with each models serving as a given level in UED.

A recent combination of the world model and Minimax Regret approach by Rigter et al. (2023) trains a world model that can derive robust policies ... These are ultimately online methods and require sufficient exploration of states that can be physically dangerous to the agent.

Sims et al. (2024) demonstrated that short rollouts (1-5 steps) can cause pathological value estimation and algorithm collapse, emphasizing the importance of full-length trajectories. Additionally, Li et al. (2024) identified inherent biases in D4RL benchmarks ... These have been very useful signals in developing an approach not reliant on traditional offline RL tricks.

notes: Central result is a tie/comparable rather than a clear win on the standard benchmark: the method only 'matches'/'achieves comparable results to online PPO' on D4RL (not clearly better). The clear advantage appears only on the authors' own newly curated (harder/unbiased) dataset where conventional offline RL underperforms. This benchmark-choice dependence and the comparable-on-D4RL framing are notable caveats; paper was rejected.
